title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 4 vs. New York Giants
headline: Arizona lost to the Giants and Mike LaFleur says Tyler Allgeier is the third-down and two-minute back. Jeremiyah Love's ankle is unresolved, and Paris Johnson (bicep), Isaiah Adams (ankle) and Hunter Long (knee) all left hurt.
summary: LaFleur opened with injuries: an unnamed player (captioned "Dewey") had a knee injury, Isaiah Adams (ankle) and Hunter Long (knee) did not return, Garrett Williams only cramped, and Paris Johnson hurt a bicep on one of the last plays. Jeremiyah Love had his ankle worked on during the game, but LaFleur had not yet spoken to him and said only that he was told Love would be fine, with more clarity expected tomorrow. Love was off the final drive because it was a two-minute situation where Tyler Allgeier is the third-down/protection back against heavy pressure. LaFleur said the Giants stacked the box after the first two drives and the run game stalled. He then blamed himself for play design on second-and-long, which came up on about four straight drives. He declined to say much about the four goal-line plays. He explained that the second-down call was a run with a run alert, but the Giants were going all-out, so it became the out route to Michael Wilson, which was intercepted. On a player who played three snaps in the third quarter (apparently "Marve", Marvin Harrison Jr.), he said his confidence was high and the move was about simplifying 13 personnel, because Trey McBride has to switch from the "X" tight end role to tight end. He did not answer the quarterback-change question in the transcript. Defensively, he was concerned about six plays of 15+ yards, pointing to zone coverage and Jameis extending plays. He also said the holding call on Dante Stills on the field goal was a case of "jerking" the opponent.

injuries.detail: Bicep injury on one of the last plays; more will be known tomorrow.
Ankle injury; did not return.
Knee injury; did not return.
Only cramps, 'no big deal'.
Ankle was being worked on during the game; LaFleur hadn't spoken to him, and will look at it more tomorrow.

signals.claim: Love's ankle will be evaluated tomorrow after he was treated during the game.
signals.note: Ankle is unresolved, so monitor the injury report before setting lineups.
signals.quote: we'll look at it a little bit more tomorrow, obviously

signals.claim: Love comes off the field in two-minute/pass-protection situations in favor of Tyler Allgeier.
signals.note: Love can be capped in obvious passing situations, and the run game stalled once the Giants loaded the box.
signals.quote: Jeremiah can obviously be out there and do it, but you want to segment

signals.claim: Allgeier is the third-down/two-minute back, with a protection emphasis.
signals.note: He has a defined situational role, which could matter more if Love's ankle is a problem.
signals.quote: Tyler being our kind of that third down back

signals.claim: A low snap count in the third quarter was about simplifying personnel in 13 sets, not a demotion.
signals.note: LaFleur backs him publicly, but the low snap count and personnel simplification make usage worth watching.
signals.quote: my confidence is high on Marve

signals.claim: McBride moves between the X and tight end roles, which complicates substitutions in 13 personnel.
signals.note: His alignment flexibility is part of why the offense simplified groupings.
signals.quote: Trey has to kind of switch his position

signals.claim: Wilson was the target on the second-down goal-line out route that was intercepted.
signals.note: He was the intended target on a key red-zone play, though the coach described it as a scheme decision.
signals.quote: we had the kind of the out route to Mike there

topics.detail: LaFleur blamed himself for play design on second-and-long, which came up on about four straight drives, and said the Giants loaded the box after the first two drives. He said the run game recovered briefly on the third drive.

Arizona went with big personnel and an out route, and the second-down call carried a run alert but the Giants were going all-out. He declined to say much beyond that and said the staff will reevaluate.
The defense gave up six plays of 15+ yards. LaFleur pointed to zone coverage and Jameis extending plays, and said the team will check the tape for breakdowns.
The holding call on Dante Stills on the field goal came from the TV copy; LaFleur said the sideline didn't see it and accepted the explanation that Stills jerked the opponent.
He called it a stinging loss, one of three losses in three weeks, and said the team has to get back to work Wednesday.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps Ravens' Win Over Titans
headline: Lamar Jackson is day-to-day with an ankle issue after Tyler Huntley closed out the win. Durham Smythe's Achilles is also a concern, and the coach had no updates on either.
summary: Minter was pleased with the 24-18 home win but called the 13 penalties (over 50 in four games) unacceptable and said the problem starts with him and his staff. Lamar Jackson left with an ankle problem. Minter said he doesn't know enough yet and that there was some talk of Jackson returning. He praised Huntley ("Snoop") for running the offense in relief. The team played more conservatively in the second half because of the weather and the lead. Another offensive lineman and a tight end (Durham Smythe, apparently an Achilles issue) went down, and a first-time center got praise for his week of prep against a strong interior opponent. Minter said more would be known tomorrow on the injured players. On defense he liked the tackling improvements and the pressure on the quarterback without Trey Hendrickson, but he wants more finished sacks. He called the roughing penalty an unfortunate timing play and credited a goal-line fourth-down stop. The kicker made the longest field goal in the stadium's history but missed a later one that would have made it a three-score game.

injuries.detail: Dealing with an ankle issue. Minter said he doesn't know enough yet and there was some talk of Jackson coming back into the game.
Left the game, apparently with an Achilles injury per the reporter. Minter said nothing right now and more should be known tomorrow.
Was not available for the game. Minter said the pass rush still affected the quarterback without him.

signals.claim: Jackson's ankle injury status will be clarified in the coming days; he could have returned to the game if needed.
signals.note: Jackson's availability next week is uncertain, which affects the QB and the whole Ravens offense.
signals.quote: I don't know enough about it right now.

signals.claim: Huntley would step in as the quarterback if Jackson cannot play.
signals.note: Huntley is the backup to roster if Jackson's ankle keeps him out, and Minter showed confidence in him.

signals.claim: Smythe's injury will be evaluated and more will be known tomorrow.
signals.note: A possible Achilles injury could open up tight end snaps for other players.
signals.quote: Nothing right now. We'll probably know a little bit more tomorrow.

signals.note: He was out for this game and the defense still got pressure, but his return timeline is unaddressed.

topics.detail: Minter called 13 more penalties unacceptable, over 50 in four games, saying it starts with him and the staff. He noted penalties on defense extended drives and said that if they stop getting in their own way there is a high ceiling.

Another lineman was lost, and a player made his first start at center against a strong opposing interior. Minter praised him and expects the film to look good, but said the run game and pass protection were not sustained enough. He described injuries as an opportunity for others to step up.

Minter said tackling improved after the first part of the game and the defense played better on third down. The pass rush affected the quarterback but didn't finish, and he wants a game like this to be a 4-6 sack performance.
The kicker made the longest field goal in stadium history but missed a later one that would have given a three-score lead. Minter said the team has confidence in him.
The Ravens played more conservatively in the second half due to the weather and the lead, and Minter said they need to put games away.

title: Joe Brady Talks The Need To Clean Up Mistakes After Loss To The Patriots
headline: Brady vows to get Dalton Kincaid more involved after a two-target game, praises Keon Coleman's stepped-up performance with DJ Moore out, and backs rookie CB Maxwell Hairston despite a rough day.
summary: Brady said the offense never found a rhythm in the 29-26 loss to New England, citing three-and-outs, including one right after a turnover, and a failure to execute against looks the team expected. He took responsibility for the final play, saying he needed a better call and protection, and he trusts Josh Allen to throw the ball away when nothing is open. He fully backed Maxwell Hairston after the young corner was targeted repeatedly, saying he won't pull a player just because he gave up plays and expects him to make those plays when targeted. He also mentioned Igbinosun as someone he trusts to roll with. He praised Keon Coleman for handling the play-calling changes after DJ Moore left the game, with a big third-down win and a touchdown, and said Allen trusts him. Brady called Dalton Kincaid's two-target game unacceptable on his end and said he must find ways to get him the ball, while crediting Allen for not forcing it. He flagged turnovers, including a fumble by Khalil Shakir in the two-minute drill and a late interception, as the thing to fix, saying protecting the ball means winning. He closed by saying the loss, his first as a head coach, should hurt, and that the team should avoid excuses and focus on self-improvement.

injuries.detail: Left the game at some point and the offense had to adjust its call sheet. Brady gave no diagnosis or timeline.

signals.claim: Coleman will be counted on to make the most of his opportunities, with Allen trusting him in key situations, especially if DJ Moore is out.
signals.note: Coleman produced a third-down conversion and a touchdown and gained trust. His volume could rise if Moore is sidelined.
signals.quote: Josh has a lot of trust in him

signals.claim: Brady will find a way to get Kincaid more targets after he saw only two in this game.
signals.note: Brady publicly took the blame for the lack of targets, which suggests a bounce-back in volume for Kincaid.
signals.quote: There's no reason Dalton Kincaid should have two targets.

signals.claim: Hairston will remain a starting corner despite being targeted heavily and struggling against New England.
signals.note: Opposing passing games may keep testing him, which is relevant for matchups against Buffalo's defense and for IDP.
signals.quote: there's a reason Maxwell Hairston's out there

signals.note: Shakir's fumble in the two-minute drill ended a big play and is part of the turnover problem Brady wants fixed.

signals.claim: Brady trusts Allen to throw the ball away when nothing is open, and says the last play was on his call and the protection.
signals.note: Brady shielded Allen from blame, but the turnovers, including a late interception, remain a concern.
signals.quote: I'm trusting that if it's not there, he'll throw it away.

topics.detail: Brady stressed that two turnovers affected the game and that protecting the football is the clearest path to winning. He said the team emphasized it during the week.
Brady defended letting the young defensive backs play through mistakes while coaching them on the sideline. He said trust is key and that a player who thinks the staff lost confidence in him is lost.
Buffalo had several three-and-outs, including one after a turnover, and did not execute against looks they expected from New England.
Brady said wins and losses feel the same to him because he is always focused on cleaning up mistakes. He said the team should avoid excuses and focus on self-improvement after its first loss.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' victory over Jets | Press Conference
headline: Tyson Bagent got the bulk of the QB snaps in the 23-12 win, and Kyle Monangai got about 30 carries with Roschon Johnson also running well. A late-game thumb injury to an unnamed player is still being checked.
summary: Johnson was pleased with the 23-12 win over the Jets, which put the Bears at 3-1. The defense was the main story: it held New York to roughly 150-160 yards and went 0-for-7 on third down. He called the unit a 'no name defense' and gave Devin Bush Jr. a game ball for his energy and a big sack. The offense held the ball for about 42:45 and finished the game with it, but Johnson said the red zone and turnovers need work, since the team has left points on the field three weeks in a row. Case Keenum got a ceremonial first snap before Tyson Bagent took the majority of the work. Johnson said Bagent has earned the number two QB job, praised his poise against pressure and his 37-yard throw to Rome Odunze before halftime, and noted one interception. Kyle Monangai carried about 30 times and ran hard, and Johnson said he wants to keep feeding him when a back is running like that. Roschon Johnson also ran well, and Johnson praised the offensive line and tight ends as blockers. Johnson opened by mentioning a thumb injury, but the transcript cut off before the player was named, and he said a later question about a player slow to get up after a fumble was not injury-related.

injuries.detail: Johnson opened by saying a player has a thumb injury that happened late in the game and is being evaluated. He hopes to have more information tomorrow. The player's name was not captured in the transcript.

signals.claim: Bagent is the Bears' number two quarterback behind the starter.
signals.note: Bagent is now the clear backup, so he is the next man up if the starting QB is unavailable.
signals.quote: Tyson has earned the right to be our our number two quarterback.

signals.claim: Monangai will keep getting a heavy workload when he is running well, after about 30 touches in this game.
signals.note: He is the lead back and got a feature-back workload, which supports his weekly volume.
signals.quote: you want to feed him as the play caller

signals.claim: Roschon Johnson remains part of the running back rotation behind Monangai.
signals.note: He is a positive-toned secondary back, but Monangai's workload leaves limited fantasy opportunity.
signals.quote: Roshan came in, came, ran super hard as well.

signals.note: Bush earned a game ball and had a big sack, a good sign for his IDP value.
signals.quote: gave a game ball to Devin Bush

topics.detail: The defense held the Jets to about 150-160 yards and 0-for-7 on third down. Johnson praised the game plan and the unselfish, assignment-sound play of the group.

topics.topic: Time of possession and offensive style
topics.detail: The Bears held the ball for 42:45 against a Jets team that had ranked first or second in time of possession. Johnson said they avoided negative plays and third-and-longs but lacked explosive plays. He also liked that they finished the game with the ball for the second week in a row.

Johnson said the red zone is a major emphasis after three straight weeks of leaving points out there, and that the offense has to cut down on turnovers. He defended kicking a field goal inside the 12 because it turned a two-score game into a three-score game.

Johnson said the roster has real depth and weekly competition for active spots. He noted a practice squad player named Davenport, who is not on the provided roster, was promoted after flashing in practice.

title: Zac Taylor: "Bounce Back Next Week" | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin) both left the 22-17 loss to Jacksonville, leaving Cincinnati with only Mitchell Tinsley and Dohnte Meyers at receiver, so expect heavy snaps for them and for Mike Gesicki and the tight ends.
summary: Taylor was disappointed after the 22-17 loss to Jacksonville that dropped Cincinnati to 2-2, but he said he believes in this team and praised how it fought. He defended Joe Burrow, saying the two interceptions were really one bad play: the first came on a hit as Burrow threw, and the second was an uncharacteristic misread on a shallow cross. Taylor said he is not concerned and would go to battle with Burrow every day. Chase was lost to a concussion by halftime and Higgins to a groin injury, which left only Tinsley and Meyers at receiver. Higgins tried to re-enter on the final drive but could not go. Taylor said the staff just had to make it work, and he credited Gesicki playing outside and the four tight ends. He said the 23 rushing yards reflected how the game went, with Jacksonville's blitz-heavy front making the run game ineffective and the pass game working. He did not rule out running 40 times next week. He also said the 23 penalties need review, and that the defense got stops but missed some tackles, including a third-and-18 conversion early.

injuries.detail: Taylor said "Concussion" when asked for a halftime update. He was lost early in the game and did not return. His availability next week was not addressed.
Taylor agreed it was a groin injury. Higgins went back in on the final drive, could not run his route after one snap, and was clearly limited. His status was not discussed further.

signals.claim: Chase suffered a concussion in the loss and is in the concussion protocol, so his availability next week is uncertain.
signals.note: Concussion protocol puts Chase's Week 5 availability in doubt, so have a backup plan.
signals.quote: Concussion. Concussion.

signals.claim: Higgins has a groin injury that he could not play through, even when he tried to re-enter on the final drive.
signals.note: He could not go even in a desperate situation, which raises real doubt about his availability next week.
signals.quote: He couldn't do it.

signals.claim: Tinsley, who recently returned to the team, played a lot of snaps and will keep a big receiver role while Chase and Higgins are out.
signals.note: He is one of only two healthy receivers left, so he is a possible deep-league or desperation add if the injuries linger.
signals.quote: he's playing a lot of snaps for us

signals.claim: Meyers was one of the last two healthy receivers and will keep a significant role while Chase and Higgins are out.
signals.note: He is a volume-dependent, speculative add if Chase and Higgins miss time.
signals.quote: they're out there making plays

signals.claim: Gesicki lined up outside as a receiver at points and could keep doing so while the wide receivers are depleted.
signals.note: Extra snaps out wide and a larger target share make him more interesting if the receiver injuries linger.
signals.quote: Mike G's playing outside receiver at points

signals.claim: Taylor is not concerned about the two interceptions and expects the pass-heavy approach to continue.
signals.note: Burrow keeps full backing from the coach and will likely keep throwing a lot, though his receiving corps is thin.
signals.quote: I'll go I'll go to battle with him every day.

topics.detail: The offense ran for only 23 yards and Taylor said that was not how he saw the game going. He said the passing game was working and the run was getting about two yards a carry in the second half. He said the team could run 40 times next game.
The team had 23 penalties, and Taylor said it felt like they went both ways. He said the staff will review the tape and clean up what it can.
After Chase went out, the under-center offense struggled to find rhythm against Jacksonville's pressure. Second-and-short was being met with third-down-style pressure.

Taylor said the defense made tackling mistakes, including allowing a third-and-18 conversion early. He said it improved over the game and made stops late to give the offense a chance. The safeties will be assessed on tape.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week 4 #DALvsHOU
headline: Cowboys beat Houston 34-30; Lamb and Pickens both feature heavily, Dak was 'flawless' in the second half, and Overshown, Tyler Smith and Joey Porter Jr. are the health items to track before Thursday at Tampa.
summary: Schottenheimer was thrilled with a gritty 34-30 win on the road in Houston, which came after the tough trip to Rio. He said the offense is hard to defend because if teams take away George Pickens or CeeDee Lamb, the other one beats you. Lamb 'played dynamite' and the ball found him a lot. Pickens made plays when he got his chances, and the coach said a fourth-quarter double move would have been a 60-yard touchdown if protection hadn't leaked against Will Anderson. Dak Prescott was praised for his grit against a very good defense and for being flawless in the second half after adjustments. The offense controlled the clock for roughly 35 minutes and ran well in the low red zone. The defense held Houston to 3-of-10 on third down and 62 rushing yards on 19 carries, though Nico Collins got loose for a big play. Joey Porter Jr. played on a pitch count after missing practice time. Overshown and Tyler Smith are 'trending positively' but won't be clear until about Tuesday. Dallas now turns to a short week against the Bucs on Thursday.

injuries.detail: Asked about 'Overshown and Smith' (captions garbled the name); the coach said he is trending positively but a clearer picture won't come until about Tuesday.
Trending positively, but the coach expects no real clarity until about Tuesday, ahead of the Thursday game.
Missed a couple of days of practice, then played on a pitch count with a limited package because he didn't know all the calls and defenses. The coach wants to review the film.

signals.claim: Lamb remains a top read in the passing game and will keep getting heavy targets.
signals.note: He is the primary target in a passing offense that the coach says has two elite options, so his target floor stays high.
signals.quote: CD played the way he always plays dynamite.

signals.claim: Pickens is on a double move in the offense and is a primary option when defenses lean toward Lamb.
signals.note: He is a big-play threat with a near 60-yard touchdown opportunity, and defenses can't take away both Lamb and him.
signals.quote: when George got his op, what's George do makes plays.

signals.claim: Prescott played well in the second half after halftime adjustments, against an elite defense.
signals.note: He handled pressure and the offense has been moving the ball consistently, which supports the whole passing game.
signals.quote: I thought he was flawless in the second half.

signals.claim: Overshown's availability for Thursday will be clearer around Tuesday.
signals.note: Short week means a late-week decision, so check the practice report.
signals.quote: both guys are trending positively.

signals.claim: Smith's availability for Thursday will be clearer around Tuesday.
signals.note: An offensive line absence on a short week could affect protection and the run game.

signals.claim: Porter played a limited role on a pitch count and may see more of the defensive package as he learns the calls.
signals.note: He is a corner returning from missed practice time; for IDP leagues, his workload is likely to grow.

signals.claim: The coaching staff wants to blitz linebackers like Barham more often.
signals.note: More linebacker pressure could lift his IDP value if the plan continues.
signals.quote: Jay, Sean's a guy you want to bring

topics.detail: Dallas held Houston to 3-of-10 on third down and 62 rushing yards on 19 attempts. The staff mixed up pressures, including linebacker blitzes. The coach said the unit is getting better, though Nico Collins burned them early.

Dallas missed a long field goal, which the coach said was pulled slightly left, and had blocks on others. He said inside gap integrity is the issue and expects it to be fixed quickly. He expressed full trust in his kicker.
Shemar James' wife is in labor and he will be flying home. The team has a short week with three games in 11 days.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'Proud of our guys' effort today'
headline: Packers beat Tampa Bay 17-14, but LB Edgerrin Cooper's outlook is 'not good', and newly arrived Kevin Zeitler didn't play; Watson and Golden flashed as big-play options.
summary: LaFleur praised the team's 60-minute effort in the 17-14 win but was blunt that the offense was not up to standard. He pointed to too many penalties, turnovers, fumbles, and critical third-down drops, and said ball carriers who keep fumbling will sit. The offense ran the ball better, which opened up play-action and some explosive plays, and Jordan Love was kept relatively clean, although the offense was often in first-and-20. On injuries, he called Edgerrin Cooper's outlook 'not good' and had no answer for how the defense replaces him. Kevin Zeitler, who had just arrived and had three practices, was held out to give him a ramp-up period, and LaFleur would only take his availability 'day by day'. The defense got credit for aggressive, repeated pressure late that kept Tampa out of field goal range, and Evan Williams drew heavy praise for his pick and edge pressure. LaFleur said Christian Watson and Matthew Golden made dynamic plays and the offense must find ways to get them the ball. He also praised Travis Glover's mentality after Glover got back on the field, while saying the line needed to get 'a little bit bigger inside'.

injuries.detail: Asked about his outlook, LaFleur said 'not good' and that he suspects the situation is serious. No specific diagnosis or timeline was given, but the team is clearly preparing to play without him.
Not injured as far as the coach said. He was held out as a ramp-up decision after joining the team this week, and LaFleur said they would take it day by day.

signals.claim: Cooper is likely to miss significant time.
signals.note: Losing a key LB changes the Packers' defensive personnel and could shift tackle and snap distribution to other linebackers.
signals.quote: Not good. I would I would suspect that, yes.

signals.claim: Zeitler will be eased into the lineup rather than starting immediately; availability is day by day.
signals.note: His arrival could affect the interior O-line and the run game, but his timeline is unclear.
signals.quote: we got to ramp him up, give him a ramp up period

signals.claim: Williams will keep being used as a disruptive weapon, including blitzing off the edge.
signals.note: His versatility (interception plus pass-rush pressure) makes him a strong IDP option.
signals.quote: he's a very intelligent football player. Really instinctive.

signals.claim: The Packers will look for more ways to get Watson the ball.
signals.note: LaFleur wants to feed him for explosive plays, which helps his big-play upside.
signals.quote: we got to find ways to continue to get the ball in their hands.

signals.claim: The Packers will look for more ways to get Golden the ball.
signals.note: He is part of the offense's explosive-play plan, which makes him more attractive as a fantasy option.
signals.quote: we got to find ways to continue to get the ball in their hands.

signals.claim: Glover is a trusted depth lineman and may keep playing on the line.
signals.note: Offensive line depth is being tested, which matters for Love's protection and the run game.
signals.quote: he's made of the right stuff. He's got the right mentality.

signals.claim: Love will keep benefiting from a run-game-driven offense that opens up play-action.
signals.note: Better protection and a more varied playbook support his outlook, though the offense is still inconsistent.
signals.quote: I thought he did a lot of great things today.

topics.detail: LaFleur was unhappy with scoring only 17 points, citing penalties, turnovers, fumbles, drops on third down, and being in first-and-20 too often. He warned that ball carriers who fumble will end up on the bench.
The run game was better, which let the offense open up play-action concepts that had been missing and produced explosive plays.
He praised the aggressive approach, noting three straight pressures that kept Tampa Bay out of field goal range. He also credited Todd Bowles' defense on the other side as stingy.
Protection was decent (only two QB hits), but LaFleur said the line needs to get 'a little bit bigger inside' to protect the quarterback better.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts vs. Commanders postgame
headline: Colts win 30-13 in London; Jonathan Taylor rode the hot hand late (Seth McGowan got 5-6 carries), Laquon Treadwell stepped up amid receiver uncertainty, and Jaylon Carlies (ribs), Arden Key and Ashton Dulin (hamstrings) are injured.
summary: Steichen opened with injury news: Jaylon Carlies (ribs), Arden Key (hamstring) and Ashton Dulin (hamstring). He praised the defense, which went 3-for-15 on third down, made a big fourth-and-one stop at midfield, forced two field goals on third-and-goal and got a takeaway from Carlies that led to a touchdown. The offense started slowly with two or three three-and-outs, and Steichen took blame for his play calling. The run game picked up in the second half, with Jonathan Taylor making big runs late to control the clock. Seth McGowan had about five or six carries, but Steichen said they rolled with Taylor as the hot hand at the end. Daniel Jones ran in a touchdown on a run-pass option in man coverage; Steichen said he has made big throws but the turnovers (reporter cited seven in four games) need cleaning up. On the receivers, Darius Slayton is still learning the offense after two weeks with the team, and Steichen said it's next man up with injuries, noting Laquon Treadwell had some good catches. He called DeForest Buckner's play lights out. Next up is a division game against Pittsburgh, with the Colts at 2-2.

injuries.detail: Listed with a rib injury; no further detail on severity or availability.
Hamstring injury; no timeline given.
Hamstring injury; no timeline given.

signals.claim: Taylor will remain the lead back and keep getting the bulk of carries when he is going well, with McGowan used as a change of pace.
signals.note: Taylor's workload stays heavy, and he was used to control the clock late while feeling good.
signals.quote: JT was rolling there, you know at the end. And he felt good.

signals.claim: McGowan will keep a small share of carries (about 5-6 this game), and Steichen will reassess week to week.
signals.note: He is a limited backup with some touches, but Taylor's hot hand cut into his share.
signals.quote: So we'll look at that week in and week out.

signals.claim: Jones needs to clean up turnovers, but the coach thinks he is doing a good job overall.
signals.note: Turnover concerns (reportedly seven in four games) limit his floor even though he adds rushing production, like his TD run.
signals.quote: he's made some big time throws.

signals.claim: Treadwell will remain involved in the receiver rotation while the group is short on healthy options.
signals.note: He gets a bump in a thin receiver room, though the coach said the ball was spread around.
signals.quote: I think tread stepped up today had some good catches.

signals.claim: Slayton is still learning the offense, and his role will be evaluated next week.
signals.note: The recent arrival isn't yet a factor; his role is unclear for now.
signals.quote: Darius is still just learning the offense getting into it.

signals.claim: Carlies has a rib injury after a big game with a takeaway.
signals.note: Matters for IDP leagues; his availability should be monitored.

signals.claim: Buckner remains an elite, every-down interior presence who did not want to leave the game.
signals.note: A strong IDP option coming off a dominant game.
signals.quote: he's playing lights out for us.

topics.detail: Steichen was very happy with the defense: 3-for-15 on third down, a midfield fourth-and-one stop, two goal-line stands that forced field goals, and a takeaway that turned into a touchdown.
The offense struggled early with multiple three-and-outs, which Steichen called very disappointing and partly on his play calling. The run game helped them turn it around in the second half.
Washington's rookie quarterback entered after Mariota left and completed some deep passes against close coverage. Steichen credited the throws but said the run defense was clean.
Steichen praised the stadium, fans and hospitality of the London game and was noncommittal on whether annual international games are sustainable.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 10/4: "Our guys worked extremely hard this week"
headline: Efton Chism III's late catch and Drake Maye's poised game-winning drive stood out in the Week 4 win at Buffalo, and Vrabel praised both.
summary: Vrabel called the Week 4 win at Buffalo a hard-fought battle and said it puts New England back in the race. He praised Efton Chism III's work ethic, saying he is in the offensive coordinator's office before 6 a.m. to learn the game plan, and credited him for stepping up in a critical moment. He said Drake Maye went toe to toe with Josh Allen, was prepared and decisive, and used his legs. He also noted turnovers and plenty of things to correct. He admitted he could have wanted a better throw to Kyle Williams before Maye came back with a better ball to Chism. Vrabel said he apologized to a player over a sideline exchange tied to an unsportsmanlike penalty and that he has to be better in those moments. He defended going for it on two early fourth downs because you have to be aggressive against Allen. The defense stopped the run and got some three-and-outs, but it was beaten by a deep shot and got little pass rush late. He said he trusts safety Craig Woodson completely after Woodson bounced back from a miscue to make a game-sealing play. He also said the defensive staff mixed man, zone and split-safety looks to manage Allen's scrambling.

signals.note: He made a key late catch and drew heavy praise for his preparation, so he may be earning a bigger role in the passing game, though his target volume is unconfirmed.
signals.quote: he's an extremely hard worker

signals.note: Vrabel praised his decisiveness, accuracy and use of his legs on the winning drive, which supports his weekly QB outlook.
signals.quote: I'm happy for him. I'm proud of him.

signals.claim: Woodson will continue to be relied on in the defensive backfield.
signals.note: Vrabel's full trust after a late game-sealing play points to a secure role for IDP managers.
signals.quote: I trust Craig with everything we've got

signals.note: Vrabel suggested a Maye throw to him was off target, so keep an eye on whether the connection improves.
signals.quote: probably would have liked a better ball to, to Kyle

topics.detail: Vrabel said he swore at an official over a call, said nothing about it was derogatory, and apologized, saying he has to be better in those moments.
He said facing Josh Allen requires aggression, and the team converted two early fourth downs.

The defense stopped the run early, forced turnovers and got key three-and-outs. Late it lacked pass rush and gave up a deep shot. The staff mixed zone, split-safety and post-safety looks rather than staying in man coverage to limit Allen's extended plays.
Vrabel said the team must keep eliminating turnovers, citing a bad snap and a dropped ball earlier in the game.

title: Exclusive: Kellen Moore Previews Saints Monday Night Football vs. Falcons
headline: Kellen Moore's Monday Night Football preview was all generalities: no injury, role, or depth chart news, just respect for an explosive Falcons offense.
summary: Moore said the team is excited to play its first Monday Night Football game in the Superdome since 2022 and to showcase the city and community. He wants players to understand the historical significance, including ties to Katrina and the Superdome's return, while treating it like any other game on the schedule. He called Atlanta a division opponent the Saints will see multiple times, and said the Falcons deserve their confidence after playing well against Green Bay last week. On leadership, he praised the steadiness of his players, who don't ride the emotional roller coaster after highs and lows. He described Atlanta's offense as explosive and capable of big plays at any moment, and said the quarterback stability will help them. He called the Falcons' defense aggressive and said it attacks the football. He gave no injury updates, depth chart changes, or player-specific usage information.

topics.detail: First Monday Night game in the Superdome since 2022. Moore wants players to appreciate the history but treat it as just another game.

Moore called Atlanta's offense explosive and capable of big plays, with quarterback stability helping. He called the defense aggressive and ball-hawking, and noted their confidence after the Green Bay game.
Moore praised the team's steadiness and said players avoid emotional swings after good or bad results from week to week.

title: Coach John Harbaugh: 'That's what winning teams do'
headline: Jameis Winston started at QB over Jaxson Dart and the offense was reshaped around him. Bryan Hudson started at center for John Michael Schmitz, but Harbaugh called it short-term.
summary: Harbaugh praised the team's resilience in a Week 4 win over Arizona. The Giants held on after a controversial pass interference call, then got a late stop and an interception to seal it. He said the offense started slowly before settling down and executing, and the defense adjusted to take away Arizona's outside runs. Jameis Winston played well apart from the turnovers, which Harbaugh said must be cleaned up, including a fumble. The coach said the offense had to be steered toward different plays because the practice reps had been built around Jaxson Dart. All three running backs ran hard, but no individual back was named. J.J. McCarthy was active as an extra QB option, with some prepared plays that went unused. Bryan Hudson started at center because John Michael Schmitz missed practice time around the birth of his child, and Harbaugh said it isn't a long-term change. The defense blitzed heavily down the stretch to speed up the quarterback, and Deonte Banks, who sat last week, made the game-clinching play. Next up is a trip to Washington.

injuries.detail: Missed a couple of days of practice, with the birth of his child cited, and Bryan Hudson started at center. Harbaugh did not describe it as an injury.

signals.claim: Winston started at QB, and the offense was reorganized toward plays that suit him.
signals.note: He has the starting job for now, but turnovers are a concern and the offense is still adjusting around him.
signals.quote: I thought he played well. You know except for the turnovers

signals.note: Dart was not the QB in this game. Harbaugh only referred to him in the past tense and gave no reason or timeline for his return.
signals.quote: you're not running some of those plays as much as when Jackson was in there

signals.claim: McCarthy was active as a third QB option for certain prepared plays but was not used in this game.
signals.note: A package for him exists but was not used, so he has no fantasy value yet.
signals.quote: It just gave us an option in case we want to put JJ out there

signals.claim: Hudson started at center this week, but this is not a long-term change.
signals.note: Offensive line continuity is a small positive, but Schmitz is expected to return to the job.
signals.quote: it's not a long term thing.

signals.claim: Schmitz sat this week after missing practice time, and the team has two centers it likes.
signals.note: The line is stable overall, but monitor his practice status next week.
signals.quote: JMS had missed a couple days of practice

signals.claim: Banks went back into the starting lineup after sitting last week and made the game-clinching play.
signals.note: The coach is backing him with a starting role, which helps IDP value.
signals.quote: But you got to trust him, you know?

signals.claim: Reese is emerging as a top defensive playmaker and may get a game ball for defensive player of the game.
signals.note: He had an interception and numerous tackles, which is IDP production that looks likely to continue. The name is inferred from the captioned 'Greece'.
signals.quote: he's taken off defensively

topics.detail: Harbaugh stressed cleaning up turnovers and ball security, including a fumble. The offense also had to find a way to get first downs rather than just run the ball.
The defense adjusted to take away Arizona's outside runs and protect the edge better. It also blitzed heavily down the stretch, as planned, to speed up the quarterback and force a quick throw.
Harbaugh credited punt coverage and punt return for field-position swings. He also praised the field goal kicker for a second straight big game.
The Giants are 3-0 at home for the first time in 18 years. Harbaugh said they can play much better and called the win a team victory.

title: HC Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (10/4) | Week 4
headline: Jets lose their third straight as 12 penalties wipe out three interceptions; Geno Smith was off-target, and Brownlee is in concussion protocol but expected to be fine.
summary: Aaron Glenn was very disappointed after the loss, saying the Jets never played complementary football. His main complaints were the penalties, which he said came mostly on third down and wiped out several takeaways, including three interceptions. The Jets took 12 penalties to the opponent's 3 or 4. The defense faced about 89 plays while the offense ran only 32 to 35, which made it hard for the offense to get anything going. Glenn said the yardage allowed (385 last week, 492 today) matters less to him than the undisciplined plays that kept drives alive. He acknowledged that Geno Smith missed some throws, high or wide on crossing routes, and said the play callers and players all need to fix it. He also said the offense must get the ball to two playmakers who were barely involved, and that opponents were doing something to roll up coverage on one of them. Glenn called the two-minute drill and the takeaway-to-points conversion (six points off a pick and a fumble) things to keep working on. On the three-game losing streak, he said he wants players to ignore the franchise's history and focus on staying positive and improving.

injuries.detail: Suffered a chest injury in the game. Glenn gave no further update, and the name does not match anyone on the provided roster.
Checked for a concussion. Glenn thinks he will be fine and he looked okay in the locker room, but he must clear the proper protocol.

signals.note: Smith was inaccurate early, missing high or wide on crossers; Glenn backed him but said the offense needs to fix it.
signals.quote: sometimes man things could be a little off

signals.claim: Brownlee is expected to be fine once he clears concussion protocol.
signals.note: His availability next week depends on clearing the protocol.
signals.quote: I think he'll be fine.

topics.detail: The Jets had 12 penalties to the opponent's 3 or 4, mostly on third down, and they extended drives. Three interceptions were nullified. Glenn said this is what he is most upset about.
The defense faced about 89 plays while the offense ran only 32 to 35. Glenn said this wore down the defense and made it hard for the offense to find rhythm.

Asked why two key playmakers were barely involved, Glenn said the opponent was trying to roll up coverage on one of them. He called them the engines of the offense and said the Jets must find ways to get them the ball. He also said a player he called 'Brandon' (the captions are unclear who) ran the ball pretty solidly. The transcript does not make clear which players he meant.

The Jets got only six points off an interception and a fumble, and they struggled in the two-minute drill, which they practice up to three times a week. Glenn said he has confidence it will come around.
The defense allowed 385 yards last week and 492 today against two good offenses. Glenn said the yardage isn't the real issue; the penalties and missed chances to get off the field are.
After a third straight loss, Glenn wants players to block out outside talk about the franchise's history and stay positive while improving.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 4, 2026
headline: Sirianni owns the failed 4th-and-2 and an offense that went 0-for-12 on third down, offered no injury updates, and said left tackle Markel Bell is dealing with a personal matter after his first start.
summary: After the 24-20 loss to the Rams, Sirianni took responsibility for a failed fourth-and-2 from the 2-yard line. He wanted to turn a two-score lead into a three-score game, and he said the failure falls on him as head coach. He repeatedly pointed to third down as the biggest problem, saying the offense was 0-for-12, and said no single cause explained it, though he needs to watch the tape. A reporter said the Rams blitzed on every third down. Sirianni did not dispute that and said the pass-protection issues had several causes. On the run game, he said he believed outside zone was called a handful more times than reporters recalled, and that gap runs complementing it also worked. He said the offense overall was not good enough and that the offense and he himself will wear the loss. He expressed confidence in Saquon Barkley as part of that discussion. He said Markel Bell is dealing with a personal matter and declined to say more, though he praised Bell's effort in his first start and said nothing stood out as Bell's fault before the tape review. He refused to use injuries as an excuse, and said the offense is still searching for its identity four games in.

injuries.detail: Sirianni said Bell is dealing with a personal matter and declined to elaborate. This is not a physical injury, but his availability is uncertain.

signals.claim: Bell started at tackle and played well in the game, though Sirianni still has to review the tape; his availability is tied to a personal matter.
signals.note: Bell's status affects the offensive line protecting Hurts and blocking for Barkley, and his availability is unclear.

signals.claim: Outside zone, which worked on Barkley's first play, will likely remain part of the run game, though Sirianni disputed that it was dropped.
signals.note: The run scheme worked early, but the offense failed to sustain drives, so Barkley's volume depends on staying in manageable downs.

signals.claim: Hurts faced a blitz on every third down in the first half and the offense converted none of its third downs.
signals.note: Pass-protection problems on third down are hurting Hurts and the passing game's reliability.

topics.detail: Sirianni went for it on 4th-and-2 from the 2-yard line while up 10 and the attempt failed. He said it was on him as head coach and that it wasn't good enough from either coaches or players. He added that the clock was running low before the snap, but there was no confusion.
The offense went 0-for-12 on third down and 2-for-9 the week before. Sirianni cited a mix of execution and coaching errors and said he would watch the tape before reacting.
After Andrew Mukuba's interception gave a short field, the offense lost yards on a run and then failed to score, which Sirianni said cost the chance to put the game away.
Sirianni said the offense hasn't been good enough and is still finding its identity. He wants it to play with detail, togetherness and toughness.
Asked about the cumulative effect of injuries, Sirianni refused to use them as an excuse and gave no new injury information.

title: Todd Bowles: ‘Find a Way to Finish’ | Press Conference
headline: Jalon Daniels will start again Thursday night vs. the Cowboys, Baker Mayfield is still expected to miss about two more games, and Bowles wants the RBs (especially Sean Tucker) more involved after an 0-4 start.
summary: Bowles spoke after the Bucs fell to 0-4 in another one-score loss, saying the team has to find a way to finish games and that the problem is on everyone, starting with him. He said a long field goal try at the end was out of the question because it was 10-15 yards too far and the wind was against them. He pushed back on blaming the offensive line for Jalon Daniels being hit, saying the ball was coming out in under 2.4 seconds and that on extra-rusher plays the quarterback has to get the hot throw out and receivers must read it correctly. Daniels, in his first start, had ups and downs but did not panic and used his legs well, and he will start Thursday night. Baker Mayfield's recovery timetable has not changed, with about two more games missed as far as Bowles knows. Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. left with an oblique injury and Bowles will know more later. Bowles said the backs, especially Sean Tucker, should be more involved, and that the staff discusses it together. He also explained that Josiah Trotter and another defender were absent on a 31-yard run because of a planned rotation. The next opponent is the Cowboys.

injuries.detail: Left the game with an oblique injury; Bowles said he will find out more later.
Recovery timetable unchanged; still likely to miss two more games from now, per Bowles.

signals.claim: Daniels will start at QB on Thursday night against the Cowboys.
signals.note: Daniels is the locked-in starter for at least the short term while Mayfield is out, which makes him a streamable QB option, especially with his rushing ability.
signals.quote: Yeah he'll be the quarterback Thursday night.

signals.claim: Mayfield will miss about two more games.
signals.note: Mayfield should stay on benches or be treated as out for the next two games, with no change in his timeline.
signals.quote: Hasn't changed yet.

signals.claim: Tucker will get more involvement, especially on short-yardage plays.
signals.note: Tucker got two short-yardage plays and Bowles wants more work for him, so he could carry some touchdown upside.
signals.quote: especially Sean getting the two short yardage plays.

signals.claim: Winfield's availability depends on the severity of his oblique injury, to be determined later.
signals.note: IDP managers should monitor his status before Thursday's short-week game.
signals.quote: It's an oblique, and I'll find out more later.

signals.claim: The RB group, including Irving, should be more involved going forward.
signals.note: Bowles wants to get the backs more touches, but the three-back split caps Irving's ceiling.
signals.quote: we got to get them in the game a little bit more.

signals.claim: Trotter is part of a defensive rotation and does not play every snap.
signals.note: Rotational snaps limit his IDP value for now.
signals.quote: we were rotating them and we got full confidence in our second group.

signals.note: Bowles praised a play by Parrish that gave the offense a chance to win late, a modest positive for IDP/defensive value.
signals.quote: Good play by him. He made a good football play.

topics.detail: Bowles repeatedly said the team is not finishing close games, all of which are one-score losses, and that everyone, starting with him, must be better at the end.
Bowles said hits on the QB are not solely an offensive line issue; on extra-rusher plays the QB must throw the hot and receivers must read it correctly. He cited the quick release under 2.4 seconds.
A late field goal try was considered but judged 10-15 yards too far with wind against them.
At 0-4, Bowles took the blame, said the team will stick together, and is focused only on beating the Cowboys next.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Titans' offense moved the ball but two turnovers and a failed four-play goal-line stand cost them against Baltimore. Rookie WR Carnell Tate (apparently, 145 yards) had a productive but error-prone day, and Cam Ward's arm talent and RPO touch drew comment.
summary: Saleh called the loss frustrating and said the game was weird. He said the offense played with a lot of energy early but shot itself in the foot with two turnovers that led to 10 Ravens points and a turnover on downs inside the 5-yard line. He described a 14-point swing when the Titans failed on first-and-goal and Baltimore then went the length of the field, and he said an explosive play late in the half pushed the deficit to 24-7. On defense he credited Lamar Jackson's off-schedule plays and Derrick Henry's explosiveness, said the run defense felt good, and took blame for a third-down pressure call and a coverage call that left Cody Barton exposed. He said Baltimore isolates the middle linebacker in coverage and that Titans linebackers were caught a couple of times. Asked about four straight runs on first-and-goal, he said the run game was going well, that he would talk with Dave about it, and that he was pleased with the preparation. He praised a young big-bodied receiver, apparently rookie Carnell Tate, who he said blocked well and had a strong statistical day despite two drops and a fumble. He also said Cam Ward's arm talent is unbelievable but that he could work on touch on a hot RPO throw. No Titans injuries were discussed.

signals.claim: Will keep a significant role as a big-bodied WR and become more consistent as he learns the offense.
signals.note: The coach is not worried about the drops and fumble and sees the rookie as a long-term piece, which supports his target volume. The reporter never named him, so the identification is inferred from the 145 yards and the rookie comparison to AJ Brown.
signals.quote: he's he's going to be a good player for a while.

signals.claim: Ward will keep getting the ball out quickly in RPO reads and should work on touch on hot throws.
signals.note: The quick-read RPO approach stays, but Ward still needs to adjust the velocity on short throws, which could affect the efficiency of the short passing game.
signals.quote: he's got such an unbelievable arm talent.

signals.claim: Barton was beaten in coverage on a play Saleh says was a poor call by him, not a player error.
signals.note: For IDP managers, Saleh put the blame on his own calls, so the coverage issue is not pinned on Barton, but the linebackers remain a target for Baltimore-style isolation.
signals.quote: that one's on me. I got to go. I got to call something better.

signals.claim: Baltimore targeted Hill by isolating the middle linebacker in coverage, and the Titans will need to vary coverages.
signals.note: IDP managers should see the coverage issue as a scheme matchup rather than a role change.
signals.quote: they isolate the mike a lot.

topics.detail: The Titans ran four straight times on first-and-goal inside the 5 and failed to score. Saleh said the run game was going well and that he would talk with Dave about the sequence and review the tape.
Two turnovers led to 10 Ravens points, and the failed goal-line stand was followed by a long Ravens drive, a 14-point swing. An explosive play at the end of the first half moved the deficit to 24-7.

Saleh was satisfied with the run defense against Henry but said Lamar Jackson's off-schedule plays and a well-designed play against the flat defender hurt. He said he picked the wrong protection to attack and the wrong pressure on a key third-and-6.
